bmi_calculator.description: Calculate your Body Mass Index (BMI) and get health advice. Supports metric and US units, instant calculation.
bmi_calculator.what_is_bmi_desc: BMI (Body Mass Index) is a value derived from the mass and height of a person. It is used to categorize underweight, normal weight, overweight, and obesity in adults.
bmi_calculator.how_to_calculate_desc: BMI = weight (kg) / [height (m)]². For US units: BMI = [weight (lb) / (height (in))²] × 703.
bmi_calculator.health_advice_desc: Maintain a balanced diet, exercise regularly, get enough sleep, and consult a doctor for personalized advice.
bmi_calculator.healthy_range: Healthy BMI range: 18.5 - 24.9 kg/m² (WHO International Standard)
bmi_calculator.input_tip: Please fill in the information. Calculation is automatic.
bmi_calculator.disclaimer: BMI is for reference only. For specific health conditions, consult a professional doctor.
bmi_calculator.page_title: Free BMI Calculator - Online Body Mass Index Calculator Tool | TinyToolFlare
bmi_calculator.page_description: Free online BMI calculator supporting metric/US units, automatic body mass index calculation, healthy weight ranges, and BMI classification. Provides adult and children/adolescent BMI standards, professional health assessment tool.
bmi_calculator.page_keywords: BMI calculator, body mass index, weight index calculation, healthy weight, online BMI tool, free calculator, health assessment, weight management, body mass index calculator
bmi_calculator.formula_note_1: Metric units: weight in kilograms (kg), height in meters (m)
bmi_calculator.formula_note_2: US units: weight in pounds (lb), height in inches (in), multiplied by conversion factor 703
bmi_calculator.formula_note_3: BMI calculation results are for reference only. For specific health conditions, please consider body fat percentage, waist circumference and other indicators comprehensively.
bmi_calculator.adult_standards_note: * Reference World Health Organization (WHO) standards. Some Asian countries set the "normal" upper limit to 23.9.
bmi_calculator.bmi_explanation: BMI (Body Mass Index) is an internationally recognized indicator for measuring human body fatness and health risks. It evaluates individual weight status through the ratio of weight to height, applicable to most adults. BMI calculation is simple and widely used in epidemiological surveys and clinical assessments.
bmi_limitations: BMI mainly reflects total body fat content and cannot distinguish between fat and muscle.
For special populations such as athletes, pregnant women, and the elderly, BMI is for reference only.
Both high and low BMI may increase the risk of chronic diseases such as cardiovascular disease and diabetes.

faq.title: Raised Bed Soil Calculator FAQ
faq.description: Answers to common questions about how much soil for raised beds, bag counts, filler, and bulk soil.

items.question: How much soil do I need for a 4x8 raised bed?
items.answer: For a 4 ft x 8 ft raised bed filled 12 inches deep, you need about 32 cubic feet of soil. That is about 1.19 cubic yards, 906 liters, or 22 bags if each bag is 1.5 cu ft.

items.question: How many bags of soil fill a raised bed?
items.answer: Divide the total soil volume by the bag volume, then round up. For example, 32 cu ft divided by 1.5 cu ft per bag equals 21.33, so you should buy 22 bags.

items.question: What depth should a raised garden bed be?
items.answer: Many vegetable gardeners plan for about 10-12 inches or more of soil depth. Some shallow herbs and greens can use less, while larger or deeper-rooted crops may benefit from more depth.

items.question: How do I calculate soil if I use filler at the bottom?
items.answer: Subtract the filler height from the total bed depth first. Then multiply length x width x remaining soil depth. The calculator does this automatically when you enable filler mode.

items.question: Should I buy soil by bags or cubic yards?
items.answer: Bags are convenient for small beds and easier to move. Cubic yards often make more sense for multiple beds or large volumes because bulk delivery can reduce cost and packaging.

uuid_generator.title: UUID Generator
uuid_generator.description: Quickly generate unique UUIDs for development, databases, and more.
uuid_generator.about_desc:
A UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) is a 128-bit number used to uniquely identify information. It is usually represented as a 32-character hexadecimal string.

UUIDs are widely used for database primary keys, distributed systems, session identifiers, unique filenames, and more, ensuring global uniqueness.

The most common version is UUID v4, which is randomly generated and virtually impossible to duplicate. UUIDs can be generated without central coordination, making them ideal for distributed environments.

wake_window_by_age_calculator.description: Enter your baby's age in months and last wake time to estimate a practical wake window range and the next nap window.

wake_window_by_age_calculator.safety_text: This is a planning helper, not medical advice. Ask a pediatrician or qualified sleep professional if your baby has feeding, growth, breathing, reflux, prematurity, or health concerns.

validation.age: Enter an age from 0 to 36 months.
validation.time: Enter a valid last wake time.

explanations.newborn: Newborn wake windows are short and can change quickly. If the nap was tiny or baby is fussy, use the earlier end.
explanations.young_infant: At this age many babies still tire quickly, so the next nap often lands soon after feeding and a short play period.
explanations.three_months: Around 3 months, many babies handle a little more awake time, but overtiredness can still arrive fast.
explanations.four_months: Around 4 months, wake windows often stretch while naps may still be uneven during sleep development changes.
explanations.five_months: Around 5 months, many babies are moving toward more predictable 3-nap days.
explanations.six_months: Around 6 months, a 2 to 3 hour wake window is common, with many babies still doing about 3 naps.
explanations.older_infant: Older infants often need longer play time before naps, especially before the second or third nap.
explanations.two_nap: Many babies in this range are settled on 2 naps, so wake windows usually need enough room for morning and afternoon sleep.
explanations.transition: This is a common 2-to-1 nap transition zone. Short naps, early waking, or skipped naps may mean the schedule needs a gentle adjustment.
explanations.toddler: Toddlers on one nap often need a longer morning before nap time and a steady bedtime rhythm.
explanations.older_toddler: Some older toddlers still nap, while others are close to dropping it. Mood and bedtime are useful clues.

faq.title: Wake Window Calculator FAQ
faq.description: Answers to common wake window by age questions from newborn months through toddler naps.

items.question: How long should a 3 month old stay awake?
items.answer: Many 3 month olds do well with roughly 75 to 110 minutes awake between sleeps. Use the shorter end after a short nap or a fussy morning.

items.question: What is a typical 6 month wake window?
items.answer: A common 6 month wake window is about 2 to 3 hours. Some babies need the lower end early in the day and a longer window before bedtime.

items.question: Should I follow wake windows or sleepy cues?
items.answer: Use both. Wake windows give a planning range, while yawning, zoning out, rubbing eyes, fussing, or losing interest can tell you to start the nap routine sooner.

items.question: What if my baby takes a short nap?
items.answer: After a short nap, try the earlier end of the next wake window. A full nap often lets baby handle a longer window.

items.question: Does this replace pediatric sleep advice?
items.answer: No. This calculator is for everyday planning. Ask a pediatrician or qualified professional if sleep issues connect with health, feeding, growth, reflux, breathing, or prematurity.

faq.title: Laundry Symbol Decoder FAQ
faq.description: Quick answers for common care-label symbols and clothing tag questions.

items.question: What does a triangle with X mean on clothes?
items.answer: A triangle with an X means do not bleach. Avoid chlorine bleach and oxygen bleach unless another label instruction clearly says otherwise.

items.question: What does the circle P laundry symbol mean?
items.answer: A circle with P means professional dry cleaning is allowed with P solvents. It is an instruction for the cleaner, not a home-washing step.

items.question: What do dots mean on laundry symbols?
items.answer: Dots usually indicate heat level. One dot is lower heat, two dots are medium or warm, and three dots are hotter, depending on whether the symbol is for washing, tumble drying, or ironing.

items.question: What do bars under a laundry symbol mean?
items.answer: Bars usually mean a gentler process. One bar means mild treatment, and two bars mean very mild treatment such as a delicate cycle.

items.question: Can this decode a care label photo automatically?
items.answer: No. This tool intentionally avoids OCR and uploads. Match the visible shapes manually, then the decoder gives a local rule-based answer.
